title: Northstar Edu conversational prototype scratchpad
notes:
Call: Northstar Education (K12 SaaS) — intro + requirements capture (2025-11-01 10:00 PT)
Attendees: Priya (RW), Ethan (RW), Samira (RW), Claire Bergen (Northstar CTO), Omar Patel (Head of Product), Mei Zhang (Platform Eng lead)
Purpose: rapid feasibility for a conversational tutor prototype (math/science Q&A + worked examples), understand constraints and next steps to propose Dedicated vs Private.

High level summary:
- Northstar wants an on-site-like experience: low latency for classroom use (teacher demo) and ability to preserve PII/student data in their cloud.
- Two phases discussed: Phase A = interactive tutor (text + simple equation rendering), Phase B = long-term session memory + analytics/insights.
- Primary concern is data residency + FERPA compliance. Strong preference for Private deployment inside their AWS account (VPC peering / Private control plane).

Requirements & targets captured during call:
- Latency targets: 100-200ms p95 for single-turn short prompts (<=512 tokens) in demo environment; production can accept up to 300ms p95 but teacher experience wants snappier.
- Throughput: expected burst up to 120 QPS during morning bell; steady-state 20-30 QPS.  Concurrency per student session ~1.2 RPS.
- Session length: multi-turn sessions, token window ~4k initially, possible future need for 16k. Need KV-cache persistence per session for up to 7 days (for homework continuation).
- Model fidelity: prefer open model with instruction-tuning and math capability. Mentioned Meta/Open models (e.g., Llama2 family) and asked about Redwood verification of hallucination regressions.
- Cost constraints: tight budget for pilot — expected ~ $3k/month infra for initial pilot. Will consider committed Dedicated pricing if ROI and usage justify.
- Security: must integrate with their Okta SSO, KMS for key management (customer-managed keys), audit logs forwarded to their Splunk workspace, and ability to disable telemetry.
- Data handling: no student data to leave their VPC. Redaction pipeline required for logs and optional on-request export.

Technical gotchas / concerns (noted):
- Model quantization vs accuracy: they specifically asked if 4-bit quantization will break math reasoning; need to give sample evals. (Action: run math prompt set on q4_0 vs fp16 and report)
- GPU selection: they have preference for AWS G5/RTX-8000 equivalents — check compatibility with Redwood Private appliance/hardware SKUs.
- Caching semantics: they want per-session persistent KV cache and ability to invalidate on teacher request; current Redwood prefix caching supports TTLs but need a UX on console to evict by session id. (Raised to product)
- Token accounting: they want per-student cost attribution; needs token-level attribution surfaced in Console broken down by route/model.
- Offline/airgap for certain districts: potential future ask — document implications (long lead time, on-prem packaging).

Immediate follow-ups (owners + tickets):
- Priya: create pilot proposal doc with rough cost bands (hosted/dedicated/private) and timeline. Link -> CONFL-edu-pilot-77 (due 2025-11-05).
- Ethan: schedule benchmark run (q4_0 quantized vs fp16 baseline) with math prompt suite; measure p95 and accuracy delta. Create JIRA JIRA-EDU-3189 (assigned Ethan). Due 2025-11-10.
- Samira: investigate KMS + Okta SSO integration checklist for Private control plane and produce SSO/KMS integration notes. Add Slack thread #edu-pilot-ops. Due 2025-11-07.
- Product: feature request for Console session eviction UI and token attribution per session -> file Feature Request (internal).

Notes to self / talking points for follow-up deck:
- Emphasize Redwood Private: customer-managed keys, VPC-only control plane, audit log streaming. Show concrete diagram: northstar-VPC <-> private-control-plane (managed) + redwood-runtime inside their account.
- Benchmark ask: include latency vs batch size curves, accuracy (macro F1 on math QA) and hallucination rate on curated prompts.
- Cost framing: show baseline pilot assuming 4x A100 equivalent (or 8x T4) for expected burst, and an alternate lower-cost configuration using quantization + batching.
- Rollout plan: start with small pilot class (50 concurrent), then expand to 1000 students over term if results good. Canary model rollouts and automatic fallback to cheaper model if latency spikes.

Unresolved questions to clarify with Northstar:
- Exact retention policy for session data and requirement for deletion on request (per-student). Are they comfortable with 7-day default?
- Any regulatory requirements beyond FERPA (state-level data residency rules)?
- Expected ratio of embedding vs generative calls (they mentioned search for homework archive + rerank — need numbers).
- Are they willing to accept hosted Dedicated (customer-dedicated in Redwood infra) if Private on their AWS is too slow/expensive for pilot?

Attachments referenced in call:
- shared slide: /confluence/edu/pilot/intro (link in linked_artifacts)
- math prompt set: github examples/pilot/math-suite (PR referenced in linked_artifacts)

Next meeting: Demo + draft SOW on 2025-11-12 09:00 PT (tentative). Claire to confirm.

Quick scratch items (brain dump):
- Try sample prompt: "Show step-by-step solution for 8th-grade linear equation 3x+5=20, explain common mistakes" — run across q4_0 to check clarity.
- Build short eval: 50 prompt pairs (teacher-written) split between algebra/physics + multi-step reasoning.
- Add monitoring hooks: model drift alerts (quality regression) tied to teacher feedback button in UI.

Finish: keep this in users area as it's early-stage. Convert to more formal pilot proposal in shared drive if Northstar signals go-ahead.

-- Priya
